Q: Java SOAP Message Content Type A:

You should first try to spot the problem: on the client or on the server ? Therefore, I suggest you to add the following JVM argument in order to dump the HTTP request details.

-Dcom.sun.xml.internal.ws.transport.http.client.HttpTransportPipe.dump=true

Using this, you should then see in the console something like:

---[HTTP request - http://localhost:8780/soap/MyService]---
Accept: text/xml
Authorization: Basic *****************==
Content-Type: text/xml; charset=utf-8
SOAPAction: "xxxxx"
User-Agent: JAX-WS RI 2.2.9-b130926.1035 svn-revision#5f6196f2b90e9460065a4c2f4e30e065b245e51e
<?xml version="1.0" ?><S:Envelope xmlns:S="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/">...

If you do see the correct value for the Content-Type error, no doubt: the error is located on the side of the service provider.

Q: How to update GLIBC_2.17 in CentOS A:

I also had to install it on Centos 6.3 just now as it's a dependency of something I needed. I looked on google for glibc_2.17 and centos and found your question. Then I looked for glibc_2.17 and Fedora and found this link http://rpm.pbone.net/index.php3/stat/3/srodzaj/1/search/libc.so.6%28GLIBC_2.17%29%2864bit%29the and RPM for Fedora labeled 'other' which was this glibc-2.17-4.fc19.src.rpm. My intent with the link was not any plug, just a reference for the one I downloaded. I clicked on the fedora glibc link and after a few clicks had it in my Download folder.

I did the following and my depencency was resolved.

$ sudo user mockbuild
$ sudo groupadd mockbuild
  groupadd: group 'mockbuild' already exists     // I happened to already have it
$ sudo rpm -ivh glibc-2.17-4.fc19.src.rpm 
warning: glibc-2.17-4.fc19.src.rpm: Header V3 RSA/SHA1 Signature, key ID ba094068: NOKEY
1:glibc                  ########################################### [100%]

Hope this helps, it's my first answer on stackoverflow.

Q: Sorting with MongoDB Java driver during aggregation pipeline by a Mutated(?) value A:

Are you asking how to sort by the "Average Vendor Transaction Sent" value? You should be able to add something like this as the next pipeline stage:

new Sort(Descending.on("Average Vendor Transaction Sent"))

If I missed where you were going, please let me know :)

Q: Is there any future for a JavaScript developer doing Gen-AI? Every single JD asks for Python — am I wasting my time? A:

Depends what you want to do.

You will never find a position that trains an ML model in JS. If you do, you shouldn't take it because that company has no idea what they're doing. JS is a frontend, use it as such. I work in ML and I use Python all the time, and the only time I've ever touched JS is to make a Civ7 bot. You're talking about a few things here so break it down:

  1. RAG is a concept that can be done in anything

  2. Agentic is a topic that can be done in anything

  3. PyTorch is a Python wrapping for torch that brings it's own stuff. It support auto-gradient tracking, distributed training, and a ton of other stuff. JS will never do this, but it shouldn't

Job descriptions are generally vague and will mimic things they see in industry. Sometimes job descriptions actually reflect what people use, but not always. So that's something to consider. Where JS/Node does shine is in the frontend. Guess how Claude Code was built? It's certainly not a Python interface.

Ultimately it depends where in the "AI stack" you want to be and what that company does. But I'll be honest with you, all of MLOps, ML training, model deployment is done in Python.
